Aria: Hi all  first week here, trying to build the inference runtime from source on my dev VM. `make all` fails during NVCC compile step: 

```
nvcc fatal   : Unsupported gpu architecture 'compute_90'
ptxas fatal : Supported registers per thread exceeded
```

I've never seen compute_90, our nodes are A100s. Any tips?

Diego: welcome Aria! :wave: compute_90 is sm_90 / Hopper; you probably pulled a CUDA toolkit that doesn't know that arch or the build flags specify it incorrectly. What does `nvcc --version` and `echo $CUDA_HOME` show inside your env?

Aria: `nvcc --version` -> CUDA 11.3, and `CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-11.3`. Host driver is 525.x (infra-bot shows). I didn't set TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST or custom CFLAGS. The repo has `cmake -DCUDA_ARCH=90` in the Dockerfile. Is that the problem?

Priya: yep. A100 uses sm_80 (Ampere) or sm_89/90 depending on HW. But CUDA 11.3 predates sm_90 support. If the Dockerfile or cmake forces 90, nvcc won't accept it. Two ways: (1) upgrade toolkit to 11.8+/12.x that supports sm_90, or (2) change build target to a compatible arch (80 or 89). For local dev I'd change to `-gencode arch=compute_80,code=sm_80` to match A100.

Sam: also the "Supported registers per thread exceeded" often comes from using an arch the compiler tries to JIT for with mismatched PTX. Once you pick a supported arch the ptxas error usually goes away. If you're building CPU-only or testing small features, you can set `BUILD_CUDA=OFF` or `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=\"8.0\"` to short-circuit.

Aria: ok I'll try editing `docker/dev.Dockerfile` where it passes `-DCUDA_ARCH=90`. Quick question: how do we decide what arch to use in repo? We have a matrix for CI?

Priya: good question. We maintain `ci/arch-config.json` listing supported arch combos. On PRs we build for `80, 86, 89` by default. We only enable 90 in a special hopper branch. File's in the repo root; docs/BUILDING.md has the canonical guidance (but it's a bit out of date). Please open a tiny PR to change dev.Dockerfile to use `${CI_DEFAULT_ARCH}` or explicit 80; we'll merge quickly.

infra-bot: [gpu-info] node-dev-12: GPU model=A100-SXM4-40GB, driver=525.85.12, CUDA compatibility=11.8+

Diego: one more subtlety: if your host has CUDA 11.8 libs and container uses 11.3 toolkit with forced sm_90, nvcc might still accept PTX but ptxas will choke. Better to align toolkit version to target arch. For local convenience we have `scripts/setup-dev.sh --cuda 11.8` which pulls matching base image.

Aria: changed Dockerfile to `-DCUDA_ARCH=80` and rebuilt; nvcc error gone but now seeing nvlink warnings and a failing link: `undefined reference to __cudaRegisterFatBinaryEnd` during `libinference.so` link. Any clue?

Sam: that usually means the CUDA toolkit runtime bits (cudart static/shared) didn't get linked. Check `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` in the link step and ensure `-lcudart_static -lrt -lpthread -ldl` ordering if linking static. Also check you're using the same `-ccbin` / gcc that matches CUDA's supported compilers. CUDA 11.x supports up to GCC 9 typically. If you're on GCC 11, use `-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/usr/bin/gcc-9` in dev build.

Aria: ahh I was on gcc-11. Switched to gcc-9 in the container and added `-lcudart_static` in the cmake link line. Rebuild started and link passed!

Priya: awesome. Can you send a quick PR that: (1) updates dev Dockerfile to use CI default arch 80, (2) documents `scripts/setup-dev.sh --cuda` usage, and (3) adds a short note about "gcc version vs CUDA" in docs/BUILDING.md? That'll save future new hires.

Aria: will do. Thanks all for the help :metal:

Diego: welcome again! if you want I can pair with you on that PR in the afternoon.

Aria: yes please, ping me at 3pm PST.
